series.title: Seoul Starter · 서울 생활
series.description: Jisoo has just moved to Seoul for a new job. Follow her first days in the city: a friendly neighbor, convenience stores, subway lines and a brand-new office.
series.style_prompt: Bright, clean Korean webtoon style with crisp line art and soft cel shading; modern Seoul streets, small red-brick apartment buildings, convenience stores, offices and subway stations; soft natural daylight, warm pastel palette, friendly expressive faces. No text, letters or speech bubbles in the image.

characters.name: Jisoo
characters.appearance_prompt: Korean woman, 28, shoulder-length straight black hair with soft see-through bangs, warm brown eyes, slim build; casual look: cream knit cardigan over a white T-shirt, light-blue jeans, white sneakers and a small tan crossbody bag; office look: navy blazer over a white blouse. Bright, slightly nervous smile.

characters.name: Minho
characters.appearance_prompt: Korean man, 28, tall, short tousled dark-brown hair, friendly crescent-shaped eyes and an easy grin; at home a gray hoodie, black joggers and slippers, outside a navy bomber jacket with earphones around his neck. Relaxed, helpful body language.

characters.name: Yuna
characters.appearance_prompt: Korean woman, 31, chin-length dark bob tucked behind one ear, small silver earrings, the same friendly crescent-shaped eyes as her younger brother Minho; office look: beige blouse, navy slacks, ID badge on a lanyard. Confident, warm, big-sister energy.

characters.name: Clerk
characters.appearance_prompt: Young Korean convenience-store clerk, early 20s, short black hair, round glasses, green-and-white store uniform vest over a white shirt, polite cheerful expression.

characters.name: Team Leader Kim
characters.appearance_prompt: Korean man in his late 40s, neatly combed short black hair with a little gray at the temples, rectangular glasses, dark suit, white shirt and navy tie; calm, kind but serious expression.

episode.title: 같이 갈까요? · Shall We Go Together?
episode.synopsis: The next morning Jisoo messages Minho on KakaoTalk to ask where she can buy everyday things, and they agree to go to the supermarket by the station together. That evening they find out they're the same age, so Minho suggests dropping the formal speech, and they switch to casual 반말.

tokens.lemma_translation: to be well, at peace (used in greetings)

bubbles.translation: Is there a supermarket near here, by any chance?

tokens.note: 혹시 softens a question: 'by any chance…?'
Target word: 근처 = the nearby area; 이 근처에 = around here.
Target word: 마트 = supermarket (from English 'mart'). In speech the particle 이/가 is often dropped.

tokens.lemma_translation: to be well, at peace (used in greetings)

bubbles.translation: There's a big supermarket in front of the station.

tokens.note: N 앞에 = in front of N.

bubbles.text: 아, 감사해요! 휴지랑 물을 사고 싶어요.
bubbles.translation: Oh, thank you! I want to buy toilet paper and water.

tokens.note: (이)랑 = 'and / with', very common in speech.
을/를 marks the object: what you buy, eat or see.
Target word: 사다 = to buy. 사고 싶어요 = I want to buy.
Target word: V-고 싶다 = to want to V.

bubbles.text: 저도 오늘 마트에 가요. 같이 갈까요?
bubbles.translation: I'm going to the supermarket today too. Shall we go together?

tokens.note: 도 = also / too: 저도 = me too, I also.
Target word: 같이 = together (pronounced 가치).
-ㄹ까요? = 'Shall we…?', a polite suggestion.

bubbles.translation: Sounds good! What time shall we meet?

tokens.note: Target word: 좋아요 = 'Good! / Sounds great!', the easiest way to agree.
에 also marks time: 몇 시에 = at what time.
Target word: 만나다 = to meet (someone).
Hours use native Korean numbers: 한 시, 두 시, 세 시 (셋 → 세 before a counter).
Target word: N 어때요? = 'How about N?', handy for making suggestions.

bubbles.translation: Okay, good. Where should we meet?

tokens.note: 에서 marks where an action happens: 어디에서 만나요? = Where do we meet?

bubbles.translation: Let's meet in front of the building!

tokens.note: The same 해요 form can be a statement, a question or 'let's …'; the context decides.
Set phrase: 알겠어요 = 'Got it / Okay', confirms you understood.
Set phrase: 이따 봐요 = 'See you later (today)'.
Target word: 재미있다 = to be fun / interesting; -었- puts it in the past.

bubbles.text: 저도요! 그런데 민호 씨, 몇 살이에요?
bubbles.translation: Me too! By the way, Minho, how old are you?

tokens.note: 저도요 = 'Me too' (polite). With friends: 나도.
몇 살이에요? = How old are you? Ages use native Korean numbers + 살.

bubbles.translation: I'm twenty-eight. What about you, Jisoo?

tokens.note: N은/는요? = 'What about N?', a quick polite follow-up question.

bubbles.translation: We're the same age! Shall we drop the formal speech?

tokens.note: Target word: 동갑 = people born in the same year, often a cue to switch to 반말.

tokens.lemma_translation: to drop formal speech, switch to 반말
tokens.note: Target word: 말(을) 놓다 = to switch to casual 반말. Always ask before you do it!

bubbles.translation: Sure! Then see you tomorrow, Minho!

tokens.note: Speech-level switch: 좋아요 → 좋아. Dropping 요 = casual speech between friends.
Friends use name + 야 (after a vowel) / 아 (after a consonant) instead of 씨.
응 = casual 'yes'; use 네 with people you speak politely to.
Set phrase: 잘 자 = casual 'good night'; the polite version is 안녕히 주무세요.
